title: Kichaka in the king's court
hookLine: Kichaka kicks Sairandhri in front of the king, and the man at the dice table tells her to go inside
carry: dharma is subtle, and Draupadi still names the wrong

lines: AN ERRAND THAT IS A TRAP.
cards: The disguises have held for months. Then the queen's brother comes to visit. His name is Kichaka.
He commands King Virata's army, and the court is a little afraid of him. He sees the maid Sairandhri and wants her. She refuses him, plainly, and tells him she's protected.
He doesn't care. He goes to his sister, the queen, and the queen sends Sairandhri to his house on an errand, to fetch wine. Draupadi knows exactly what this errand is.

teach.b: At Kichaka's house he grabs at her. She breaks free and runs, straight into the royal court, where King Virata sits with Kanka at the dice.
Kichaka chases her in, catches her by the hair, and kicks her to the floor in front of everyone.
Bhima is there, and his face darkens; he stares at a big tree as if he means to tear it up for a club. Yudhishthira sees it, presses Bhima's toe, and says something like: looking for firewood, cook?
Cut your trees somewhere else. But Draupadi doesn't stay quiet.
From the floor she speaks to the king in his own court. What kind of king lets a woman be struck in front of him and does nothing?
Then Kanka turns to her. Go to the queen's rooms. Your Gandharva husbands will act when the time is right.
One word of recognition and the whole year is lost.
Here is a teaching the Mahabharata returns to again and again: dharma is subtle. In the dice hall, when Draupadi asked her question, Bhishma told her the way of dharma is subtle and hard to see.
Here two duties pull apart: the promise to stay hidden, and a husband's duty to protect.
The epic doesn't pretend it's tidy, and it gives Draupadi the voice that names the wrong: a king's power exists to protect, the heart of raja dharma, the ruler's duty.
Today, when duties collide, the epic won't let you call the cost nothing, and it won't let anyone silence the one who names the wrong.

how: The Kichaka episode is retold and staged in Indian performance traditions, and readers of the epic discuss Yudhishthira's restraint and Draupadi's protest side by side.

o: the hall where the Pandavas first lost at dice
the Matsya king, whose court sees Sairandhri struck
the general who commands the Matsya army

games.q: in Virata's court — tap the pairs.

s: Kichaka was a stranger to the royal family
he was Queen Sudeshna's brother and commanded Virata's army.
Draupadi stayed silent after she was struck
she spoke to the king in his court and asked what kind of justice this was.
Yudhishthira stopped Bhima with a remark about firewood
in his role as Kanka he told the 'cook' to find his trees elsewhere.

games.q: you're Yudhishthira, disguised as Kanka. your wife is struck in front of you. if you're recognized, the exile starts over. what do you do?
o: stand up and reveal who you are.
send her to the queen's rooms and say the time will come.
leave the court without a word.
games.why: he keeps the disguise and even stops Bhima. the epic calls dharma subtle: two duties collide here, and it lets us see exactly who pays.

practice: Let your hands rest open on your knees, and bring to mind a moment when you had to hold back, or when you wished someone had spoken for you; don't relive it, just let it be named.
Breathing in, feel how much holding back weighs, and breathing out, let your hands stay open. If you pray, you can bring the people who carry that kind of weight into your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Virata. The king whose court sees a maid struck and stays still, and the place where Draupadi asks what kind of justice that is.

carryVoice: Your line: dharma is subtle, and Draupadi still names the wrong. Struck to the floor, she still asked for justice. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Virata Parva (Kichaka-vadha), Kichaka's desire for Sairandhri, the errand for wine, the assault in Virata's court, Kanka's words and Draupadi's protest
